Alexander Ovechkin.text: The only player to score 200 or more goals in three different decades.
Alexander Ovechkin.evidence: He is the only player to have tallied 200 or more goals in three different decades, with 245 in the 2000s, 437 in the 2010s, and 247 in the 2020s.

Wayne Gretzky.text: Liked to set up behind the opponent's net, an area nicknamed "Gretzky's office".
Wayne Gretzky.evidence: Gretzky became known for setting up behind his opponent's net, an area that was nicknamed "Gretzky's office".

Gordie Howe.text: Came out of retirement in his mid-40s to play alongside his sons Mark and Marty.
Gordie Howe.evidence: Howe retired for the first time in 1971 and was immediately inducted into the Saskatchewan Sports Hall of Fame that same year. He was then inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame the following year but came back two years later to join his sons Mark and Marty on the Houston Aeros of the WHA. Although in his mid-40s, he scored over 100 points twice in six years, won two straight Avco World Trophies (1974 and 1975), and was named most valuable player in 1974; he scored a total of 174 goals in the WHA.

Jaromir Jagr.text: With 37 professional seasons and over 2,000 games, he has had the longest career in pro hockey history.
Jaromir Jagr.evidence: Having played in 37 professional seasons (as of 2024) and over 2,000 professional games, Jágr has had the longest playing career in professional ice hockey history.

Brett Hull.text: He and his father Bobby were the first father and son to each reach 600 goals or 1,000 points in the NHL.
Brett Hull.evidence: Hull was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2009, joining his father Bobby Hull. They are the first father-son combination to each score either of 600 goals or 1,000 career points in the NHL.

Marcel Dionne.text: Has the most goals of any player who never reached or won a Stanley Cup.
Marcel Dionne.evidence: His 731 goals rank as sixth most in NHL history and is the most for a player who never reached or won a Stanley Cup.

Phil Esposito.text: In 1991 he and his brother Tony co-founded the Tampa Bay Lightning, the first NHL team in Florida.
Phil Esposito.evidence: In 1991, he and brother Tony co-founded the Tampa Bay Lightning, the first NHL team in Florida.

Mike Gartner.text: Scored 30 goals in a record 15 straight seasons, yet never won a major award or reached a Stanley Cup Final.
Mike Gartner.evidence: With his blazing speed and shot, Gartner became a dependable player for the then-fledging franchise, recording the first of a record fifteen consecutive 30-goal seasons in 1979; he peaked in goals with 50 in the 1984–85 season. ... While Gartner never won a major award or reached the Stanley Cup Final as a player, he recorded over 700 goals and 600 assists in over 1,400 games, a mark achieved by only five players at the time he retired.

Mark Messier.text: The only player to captain two different teams to Stanley Cup championships.
Mark Messier.evidence: He is a six-time Stanley Cup champion—five with the Oilers and one with the Rangers—and is the only player to captain two teams to Stanley Cup championships.

Steve Yzerman.text: Named Red Wings captain at 21, he retired as the longest-serving captain in North American major league sports.
Steve Yzerman.evidence: Prior to the 1986–87 season, at age 21, Yzerman was named captain of the Red Wings and continuously served for the next two decades (dressing as captain for over 1,300 games), retiring as the longest-serving captain of any team in North American major league sports history.
